model_claims.text: fields() returns the same result for normal attrs classes as before the PR.
model_claims.source_quote: - Fast-path isinstance(cls, type) with direct getattr(cls, "__attrs_attrs__", None) lookup before calling get_generic_base(cls), avoiding unnecessary function calls on normal *attrs* classes.

model_claims.text: asdict() and astuple() fall back to fields() only when __attrs_attrs__ is None on the instance's class, preserving previous behavior.
model_claims.source_quote: - Look up __attrs_attrs__ directly on inst.__class__ (falling back to fields() only when None).

model_claims.text: asdict() and astuple() determine whether a field value is an attrs class by checking __attrs_attrs__ on type(v) directly, yielding the same result as before.
model_claims.source_quote: - Check getattr(value_type, "__attrs_attrs__", None) is not None directly on type(v) instead of calling has() / get_generic_base() (since type(v) is always a concrete class, never a _GenericAlias).

model_claims.text: astuple() no longer calls type(j) then j.__class__ and has() but still produces the same tuple output.
model_claims.source_quote: - In astuple(), avoid calling type(j) followed by j.__class__ and has().

model_claims.text: When retain_collection_types=False and the collection factory is list, asdict()/astuple() return the same list as before without extra wrapping.
model_claims.source_quote: - When the target collection factory is list (retain_collection_types=False), assign/append the list comprehension result directly instead of wrapping it in list([...]) and entering try ... except TypeError.

model_claims.text: When the dict factory is dict, asdict() returns the same dict as before but using a dict comprehension instead of dict(generator).
model_claims.source_quote: - When the dict factory is dict, use a dict comprehension {k: v for ...} instead of dict((k, v) for ...), eliminating generator frame and 2-tuple allocations per entry.

model_claims.text: attrs.asdict runs about 1.25x faster (20.3% less time) after the PR on the benchmark scenario.
attrs.astuple runs about 1.96x faster (48.9% less time) after the PR on the benchmark scenario.
attrs.fields runs about 1.39x faster (28.0% less time) after the PR on the benchmark scenario.
